# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 15 | **Condition:** moderately preserved

---

**15:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have given me insight into Your truth and knowledge of Your wonderful secrets,

**15:2** and Your covenant-faithfulness to the man of [...] and the abundance of Your mercies to the one of perverse heart.

**15:3** Who is like You among the gods, O Lord? And what is as Your truth?

**15:4** And who is righteous before You when he enters into judgment? Not any spirit

**15:5** can reply to Your rebuke, and no one can stand before Your anger.

**15:6** But all the sons of Your truth You bring before You in forgiveness,

**15:7** to purify them from their transgressions in the abundance of Your goodness and in the multitude of Your mercies,

**15:8** to cause them to stand before You forever and ever.

**15:9** For You are an eternal God, and all Your ways are established forever and ever,

**15:10** and there is none besides You. And what is the man of emptiness and the master of vanity,

**15:11** that he should understand Your great wondrous deed?

**15:12** And the thing formed of clay, kneaded with water -- what counsel does it understand?

**15:13** What can it plan without Your good pleasure? And what can it think without Your will?

**15:14** You have spread out all the foundations of truth and the storehouses of understanding together with the crucibles of knowledge,

**15:15** for You have opened for me a source of knowledge and fountains of understanding,

**15:16** the marvels of counsel through the strength of Your holy spirit. You have opened within me knowledge

**15:17** in the mystery of Your understanding and the spring of Your might [...] and a path of truth

**15:18** for the lowly of grace [...] to walk in all Your ways.

**15:19** And You, my God, You have put in the mouth of Your servant understanding,

**15:20** and upon his tongue You have set words, and You have established [...] from the source of Your understanding,

**15:21** to proclaim to a creature of dust according to his understanding and to interpret these things

**15:22** to one born of woman according to the measure of his insight. But I, dust and ashes,

**15:23** what can I plan unless You have desired it? And what can I think apart from Your will?

**15:24** What strength can I summon unless You have sustained me? And how can I have insight unless You have formed it for me?

**15:25** What can I speak unless You have opened my mouth? And how can I answer unless You have given me understanding?

**15:26** Behold, You are prince of the gods, and king of the glorious ones, and lord of every spirit,

**15:27** and ruler of every creature. Apart from You nothing is done,

**15:28** and nothing is known without Your will, and there is none besides You.

**15:29** And there is none with You in strength, and nothing before Your glory,

**15:30** and Your power has no price. And who among all Your great and wonderful creatures

**15:31** can retain the strength to stand before Your glory?

**15:32** And what then is he who returns to his dust, that he should retain strength?

**15:33** Only for Your glory have You done all these things.

**15:34** [...] for all the sons of Your truth [...] in the period of Your goodness,

**15:35** and in the lot of Your truth You have cast them [...]

**15:36** to make them know [...] in the community of jubilation, and Your holy spirit [...]

**15:37** and to purify them from transgression for the sake of Your great goodness [...].

---
*EMET notes: Column 15 is a hymn on the theme of knowledge originating solely from God. The rhetorical questions in lines 3-5 echo the Song of the Sea (Exodus 15:11). Lines 22-25 form a stunning catena of human dependence. "Prince of the gods" (sar ha-elim) in line 26 is a bold divine title.*
